question.text: In an experiment to find emf of a cell using potentiometer, the length of null point for a cell of emf <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. If this cell is replaced by another cell of emf <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math>. the length-of null point increases by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.

solution.text:
We know, the condition where the galvanometer shows a null point is,

E1E2=l1l2

So, 1.5E2=6060+40=610=35

⇒E2=52 V

Hence, the value of x=25.
